item.content:encoded:

They join more than 25 services you can already connect, like Slack, Figma, and Sentry. To see the full list, open Customize in the Copilot app or browse the Copilot customization page.

New services you can connect

  • Box: Search and manage content, and use Box AI.
  • Buildkite: Work with pipelines and builds.
  • Calendly: Manage scheduling and meetings.
  • ClickUp: Track tasks and projects.
  • Mixpanel: Explore product analytics.
  • Supabase: Work with projects and databases.
  • Webflow: Manage sites and content.
  • Wix: Manage sites and business tools.

item.title: Gemini 4 Neon in GitHub Copilot
item.dc:creator: Allison
item.description:
Gemini 4 Neon is now generally available in GitHub Copilot. It is designed for agentic coding, multistep tool use, and knowledge work. According to Google, Gemini 4 Neon delivers quality…

The post Gemini 4 Neon in GitHub Copilot appeared first on The GitHub Blog.
item.content:encoded:
Gemini 4 Neon is now generally available in GitHub Copilot. It is designed for agentic coding, multistep tool use, and knowledge work. According to Google, Gemini 4 Neon delivers quality close to Gemini 4 Carbon at a lower token cost per task. Google also reports that, compared with Gemini 4 Carbon, it starts responding faster and makes fewer unrequested changes on coding tasks. It is also less likely to make unsupported claims about code, tool, or test results.

This model is billed at provider list pricing under usage-based billing. See Models and pricing for GitHub Copilot for details.

Availability in GitHub Copilot

Gemini 4 Neon is available to Copilot Pro+, Max, Business, and Enterprise users. You can select the model in the model picker in:

  • Visual Studio Code
  • Visual Studio
  • Copilot CLI
  • GitHub Copilot coding agent
  • GitHub Copilot app
  • github.com
  • GitHub Mobile on iOS and Android
  • JetBrains IDEs
  • Xcode
  • Eclipse

item.title: Customize GitHub Copilot for your team
item.dc:creator: Allison
item.description:
You can now share the GitHub Copilot plugins your team relies on without asking every member to repeat the same setup. Team customizations are generally available for organization teams. Team…

The post Customize GitHub Copilot for your team appeared first on The GitHub Blog.
item.content:encoded:
You can now share the GitHub Copilot plugins your team relies on without asking every member to repeat the same setup. Team customizations are generally available for organization teams.

Team maintainers and organization owners can select approved Agent Plugins as team defaults. This gives your team a shared starting point between individual customization and organization-wide policy.

Set up plugins for a team

If you’re a team maintainer or organization owner, open your organization team on github.com and select the Customize Copilot tab. From there, you can:

  • Browse plugins from the marketplaces built into Copilot, your enterprise’s marketplaces, and any marketplaces the team adds. You can then add individual plugins to the team.
  • Add a marketplace from a GitHub repository that contains a plugin marketplace. This makes its plugins available to browse. You can add individual plugins to the team to enable them.

Selected plugins are enabled by default for the team’s direct members in VS Code, the GitHub Copilot app, and Copilot CLI.

item.title: OpenAI’s GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol now available
item.dc:creator: Allison
item.description:
OpenAI’s GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol are now generally available in GitHub Copilot. Both models are designed for agentic coding and code review, with stronger coding judgment than earlier GPT-6…

The post OpenAI’s GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol now available appeared first on The GitHub Blog.
item.content:encoded:
OpenAI’s GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol are now generally available in GitHub Copilot. Both models are designed for agentic coding and code review, with stronger coding judgment than earlier GPT-6 models. In early testing, both caught significantly more real issues in code review than earlier GPT-6 models while using fewer tokens.

  • GPT-6.2 Astra: OpenAI’s latest Astra model for agentic coding and terminal work. In early testing, it caught significantly more issues in code review than GPT-6 Astra and completed agentic coding tasks using noticeably fewer tokens.
  • GPT-6.2 Sol: OpenAI’s latest Sol model for complex agentic coding and in-depth code review. In early testing, it caught nearly twice as many real issues in code review as GPT-6.1 Sol while keeping its findings accurate.

These models are billed at provider list pricing under usage-based billing. See Models and pricing for GitHub Copilot for details.

item.title: GitHub Copilot Fusion updates: more availability, benchmarks, and models
item.dc:creator: Allison
item.description:
Today, we’re expanding GitHub Copilot Fusion with new models, available on more Copilot surfaces, and results on two public Terminal-Bench leaderboards, giving you more ways to use Fusion and compare…

The post GitHub Copilot Fusion updates: more availability, benchmarks, and models appeared first on The GitHub Blog.
item.content:encoded:
Today, we’re expanding GitHub Copilot Fusion with new models, available on more Copilot surfaces, and results on two public Terminal-Bench leaderboards, giving you more ways to use Fusion and compare its performance.

GitHub Copilot Fusion joins public Terminal-Bench 4.1 leaderboard

Copilot Fusion is now listed on Terminal-Bench 4.1 public leaderboards hosted by Stanford, Harbor, and the Laude Institute: Terminal-Bench 4.1 measures how well AI agents complete hard, realistic tasks in a terminal.

On Terminal-Bench 4.1, Copilot Fusion Max achieved a 71.2% resolution rate, 5.4 percentage points ahead of leading frontier models Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.2, while costing 88% less than Fable 5.2 and 57% less than Opus 5.5.

item.content:encoded:
Copilot is most useful when it can work where you do. The GitHub Copilot app now supports your Azure DevOps repositories, your GitHub Enterprise Server instance, and the browser you’re already signed in to.

Work with Azure DevOps repositories in the GitHub Copilot app

Clone an Azure DevOps repository, ask an agent to create a branch, make code changes, and open a pull request, then see it through to completion without leaving the GitHub Copilot app. Track its status in the sidebar, click Fix on a review comment to have an agent address it, or turn on agent merge to let an agent fix CI failures and complete the pull request once your Azure DevOps checks and policies pass.

item.title: Copilot code review: Adaptive effort, secret detection, and more
item.dc:creator: Allison
item.description:
GitHub Copilot code review now helps you catch more issues earlier, with less effort. Adaptive matches review depth to each pull request, so routine changes get a quick pass and…

The post Copilot code review: Adaptive effort, secret detection, and more appeared first on The GitHub Blog.
item.content:encoded:
GitHub Copilot code review now helps you catch more issues earlier, with less effort. Adaptive matches review depth to each pull request, so routine changes get a quick pass and risky changes get a deeper look. Reviews can also draw on related repositories and flag exposed secrets before they reach your main branch. Features in public preview are subject to change.

Adaptive, cross-repository context, and secret detection are available to Copilot Pro, Pro+, Max, Business, and Enterprise plans.

🎯 Adaptive: The right review effort for each pull request

Today, someone has to decide in settings or when requesting a review, what review effort level each pull request needs. A documentation update may only need Lite, while a change to authentication logic benefits from Max. Adaptive makes that choice for you. item.title: MAI Code 2 and MAI Code 2 Flash in GitHub Copilot
item.dc:creator: Allison
item.description:
The next generation of Microsoft AI (MAI) coding models has arrived in GitHub Copilot. Introducing MAI Code 2 and MAI Code 2 Flash, two new models that represent a major…

The post MAI Code 2 and MAI Code 2 Flash in GitHub Copilot appeared first on The GitHub Blog.
item.content:encoded:
The next generation of Microsoft AI (MAI) coding models has arrived in GitHub Copilot. Introducing MAI Code 2 and MAI Code 2 Flash, two new models that represent a major step forward for the MAI-Code family, expanding from lightweight coding assistance to complex, agentic software engineering.

  • MAI Code 2: A powerful, general purpose coding model built to help developers get from request to result with focused responses, practical code changes, and less unnecessary back and forth. Ideal for complex tasks like deep debugging, multi-file implementation, refactoring, and repository-wide reasoning.
  • MAI Code 2 Flash: A lightweight, cost-efficient coding model optimized for everyday development workflows. Well suited for code explanations, targeted edits, routine fixes, and rapid iteration.

Both models are designed for agentic coding workflows, giving developers more flexibility to choose the model that best fits their task.

Read the MAI Code 2 and MAI Code 2 Flash announcement for a deeper look at the model’s vision support, coding performance improvements, and efficiency gains.

item.title: Monitor GitHub Copilot activity through Microsoft Agent 365
item.dc:creator: Allison
item.description:
Enterprises can now stream GitHub Copilot agent activity directly into Microsoft Agent 365. This lets you bring audit data from across GitHub Copilot clients into Microsoft’s agent control plane, where…

The post Monitor GitHub Copilot activity through Microsoft Agent 365 appeared first on The GitHub Blog.
item.content:encoded:
Enterprises can now stream GitHub Copilot agent activity directly into
Microsoft Agent 365. This lets you bring audit data from across GitHub Copilot clients into Microsoft’s agent control plane, where you can review Copilot activity alongside other AI workloads.

With this release, administrators can:

  • See activity across Copilot clients, including cloud agents on GitHub.com, Copilot CLI, Visual Studio Code, Visual Studio, and partner IDEs such as JetBrains and Eclipse.
  • Review user sessions, including prompts, responses, and tool calls, and view usage trends in Agent 365.
  • Access additional risk information in Microsoft Purview and Defender to investigate and mitigate risk.

This is available for GitHub Enterprise Cloud customers with Enterprise Managed Users. To get started, see Streaming the audit log for your enterprise on GitHub Docs.
